summary:
Mission Forge, is an interactive educational space craft designing game. The players are supposed to make their own space crafts from the available set of components, which is tailored for a specific mission they are given/chosen. 
This helps more people to get familiar with the basic idea and trade-offs in designing a space craft.
details:
Mission Forge — Project Details

Mission Forge is an interactive educational space mission design game that turns spacecraft engineering concepts into hands-on experimentation.

What it does and how it works

Players design their own virtual spacecraft by selecting and assembling modular components such as solar panels, batteries, cameras, communication antennas, and onboard computers. Each component has engineering properties, including mass, power generation, power consumption, battery capacity, and cost.

The game continuously evaluates the spacecraft configuration and displays engineering metrics and mission requirement progress. Players can save and restore designs, experiment with different combinations, and launch even incomplete spacecraft configurations.

After launch, a simplified orbital simulation visualizes the spacecraft moving around Earth. It models sunlight exposure, Earth's shadow, solar power generation, battery behavior, observation activities, and communication opportunities. Live telemetry and event logs help players follow the mission. Simulation controls allow players to pause, resume, and change the simulation speed.

Benefits and intended impact

Spacecraft engineering involves interconnected systems, and changing one subsystem can affect the entire mission. Mission Forge makes these relationships easier to explore through visual and interactive learning.

Instead of simply telling players which components are required, the game allows them to experiment, make mistakes, observe the consequences, and improve their designs. It aims to encourage curiosity about space technology, systems engineering, physics, and satellite missions.

Creativity and innovation

A key design decision is that the game does not enforce one predefined spacecraft configuration. Players have freedom to experiment with incomplete or unconventional designs. The simulation evaluates available capabilities and demonstrates their consequences rather than requiring a fixed component checklist.

The connection between orbital sunlight, Earth's shadow, solar generation, battery storage, and spacecraft operations adds an interactive engineering dimension to the experience.

Technologies used

  • Python for engineering calculations and simulation logic.
  • Flask for the backend and API.
  • JavaScript, HTML, and CSS for the interactive frontend.
  • Vite for frontend development and building.
  • SVG for spacecraft and orbital visualizations.
  • Browser localStorage for saving spacecraft designs.

Factors considered

The prototype focuses on accessibility, experimentation, visual feedback, and the relationships between spacecraft subsystems. Component parameters and orbital behavior are simplified for educational gameplay and are not intended to represent exact specifications of real spacecraft or a high-fidelity orbital propagator.

Mission Forge is designed to grow through additional spacecraft components, mission objectives, and increasingly detailed engineering simulations.
